You think your organization is fine.


Claims are going out. Payments are coming in. Funding is in place.

Sonda Kunzi and Gary Humble take a direct look at what’s actually happening inside behavioral health organizations.

From Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payer challenges to credentialing breakdowns, audit risk, and the realities of grant and board funding, they connect the dots between how services are delivered—and how organizations actually survive.


Based in Ohio with experience across multiple states, they focus on what doesn’t change: the fundamentals that drive compliance, financial stability, and long-term success.


If you’re leading, managing, or responsible for the business side of behavioral health, this is the conversation you should already be having.

No hype. No tool tutorials. Just honest conversations about how senior leaders actually think with AI, and where it still can't follow.

The thesis is simple and stubborn: the next decade of work won't be won by the leaders who automate the most. It will be won by the ones who stay most human while everything around them changes.

If you're BIPOC, in therapy, thinking about therapy, or just tired of wellness content that skips the nuance, COLORS OUT LOUD is for you.

Hosted by the therapists of Colors of Austin Counseling, this weekly mental health podcast brings clinical insight out of the therapy room and into your ears. COLORS OUT LOUD brings unscripted conversations beyond the therapy couch with a healthy dose of joy, because healing doesn't have to be heavy to be real.

Each week, expect a mix of solo clinician takes, guest interviews, and roundtable conversations on grief, identity, burnout, relationships, and the mental health topics — plus recurring segments like *Ask a Clinician* and *One Next Step*, so you always leave with something to try.

title: Chronic Effects of Long COVID- Perspective from Patient and Nurse
author: Annalyssa
description:
"From Bedside to Bedridden: A Nurse's 18-Month Fight for a Diagnosis"
As a nurse, I spent years catching what others missed in patients. Then long COVID left me with racing heart rates, falls, and fatigue no one could explain — and I became the patient no one believed. It took 18 months of pushing for answers to get diagnosed with dysautonomia. The diagnosis brought grief for the body I used to trust, but also clarity. If your body says something's wrong and the tests say "normal," don't stop pushing. Be your own advocate — no one knows you like you do.

description:
So many entrepreneurs and leaders are carrying pressure no one sees. They are growing businesses, managing teams, raising families, navigating relationships, making money decisions, holding communities — and still trying to become the fullest version of themselves.

​

From the outside, they look capable. Inside, they may be exhausted, disconnected, overextended, or quietly wondering how long they can keep moving this way.

​

The Grounded CEO exists because what happens inside the entrepreneur does not stay inside the entrepreneur. It affects the business. It affects the team. It affects the body. It affects the relationships. It affects the home.

This show creates space for the conversations most leadership rooms skip — the ones about grief, capacity, control, loss, faith, ambition, rest, empathy, identity, and the inner work required to build something that can actually last.

author: Paige
description:
Hi everyone! My name is Paige, and I am a new mom trying to figure it all out just like you guys! I am trying my best, and of course (as many new parents) I am terrified, lost, and trying all the same. I never would have thought me being a mother would have been possible so early in my life. With that, it is no secret I am single mother doing this parenthood gig all alone, and I think this is a huge learning experience not just for me but for my child as well. I had so much self doubt, hurt, pain, and anger but I realized I am not the only suffering with this particular situation as myself. As we know and grow, parenthood is one of the hardest jobs there is and I cannot stress that enough! On that note, I created a podcast for parents to relate and come together when needed! 


This podcast is for all kinds of mothers, and even fathers taking on the motherhood role. As a new single mom and the only parent to my little one, I wanted to create an outlet for mothers, and other parents that can relate to my position. We explore the beautiful yet challenging journey of motherhood. Whether you’re a first-time mom or just looking for some insights, I hope you find this podcast helpful, relatable, and your new go-to for advice and insights. Just remember, you're not alone and there are people who can relate to you; whether you think so or not!! Much love, and can't wait to meet you!!

description:
Be The Bag Live is for the woman on a mission who is tired—not tired of dreaming, creating, or wanting more, but tired of chasing everything outside herself while quietly wondering, “Is this really the life I want?”

Hosted by April, this is where we have honest, funny, grown-woman conversations about self-connection, identity, work, creativity, money, boundaries, and building something that actually feels like you. Through personal stories and the Be The Bag framework—Pause, Reflection, Discernment, Experimentation, Evidence, and Revision—we’re learning to stop outsourcing our clarity and start trusting ourselves again.

There’s no performative hustle here, no pressure to have the perfect plan, and absolutely no requirement to pretend you care about things you do not care about. Just thoughtful conversations, practical questions, and plenty of permission to change your mind as you learn more about yourself.


Come in, have a seat, sip something good, and let’s talk about what it means to stop chasing the bag—and remember that you are the source, the asset, and the blueprint.

What if living longer isn’t just about adding years to your life — but adding more life to your years?

Penney for Your Thoughts explores the science of longevity, mindset, women’s health and healthy aging — and the practical things we can do to feel, think and live better at every stage of life.

Hosted by Penney Megginson, a neuroscience-informed health and performance expert with a background in physiotherapy and exercise physiology, the podcast brings together conversations with doctors, scientists, researchers and innovators alongside practical, science-backed tools you can experiment with in your own life.

It’s also home to Glowgevity — Penney’s approach to longevity built around a simple idea: longevity isn’t just about adding years to your life; it’s about adding life to your years. Glowgevity explores how the way we think, move, manage stress and experience life can influence not only how long we live, but how well we live.

From nervous system regulation, stress and the brain to menopause, hormones, movement, biohacking, emotional wellbeing and healthspan, Penney asks the questions that turn complex science into practical strategies for everyday life.

Live longer. Live better. Glow longer.

Welcome to Penney for Your Thoughts.

description:
The scary headlines never stop. What's rarely told is what happens after - the survivor who discovers resilience they didn't know they had, who transforms their darkest pain into purpose, who chose to keep going when giving up would have been easier.
Survivor Stories was born from a simple need, to feel seen. To hear from real survivors who are doing the work day in and day out, often at great personal cost to them and the ones they love. To create a safe space where conversations aren't cut short, where vulnerability is met with understanding, and where every survivor's story is valued.
Hosted by Emma Kay, Founder of WalkSafe and a survivor herself, this podcast centres on human resilience, not tragedy. How did survivors transform their deepest pain into purpose? Why did they keep going when they could have stopped? What does it feel like to lose someone and dedicate your life to their memory? These are the conversations that change how you see survival.
Through these intimate conversations, you'll discover how ordinary people do extraordinary things. How they transform trauma into advocacy. How they keep their loved ones' memories alive. And how, even in the darkest moments, they found reason to keep going. This podcast celebrates their work, their resilience, and their humanity.
If you've ever felt invisible, or if you want to truly understand the power of human survival, this is for you. This is a warm, unhurried space to listen, connect and feel less alone. And maybe to remember that your story matters too.

Lauren Goldstein is who 7- and 8-figure business owners call when they’re stuck in the weeds of success and need their business to truly run without them.

As an award-winning business advisor and consultant, and founder of Golden Key Partnership, she has spent over 15 years behind the scenes of high-growth small businesses untangling operational chaos and fixing broken team dynamics.

The Biz Doctor®, ranked globally in the top 3% of podcasts, brings those same unfiltered insights and world renowned diagnostic tactics to business owners navigating the messy millions of success.

This show is dedicated to the Operator to Owner Shift: the transition from being the engine of your business to the one who actually gets to drive it.

It’s about moving from drowning in the day-to-day to having the capacity to work on the business, rather than just in it, so you can have a business that fits around your life, instead of the other way around.

Each week, Lauren explores the nuances of sustainable scaling through three critical pillars:

Leadership: Addressing the mindset shifts necessary to move from firefighter to effective leader. Lauren focuses on helping you master delegation and communicate more effectively so the business can operate without you constantly getting pulled back into the weeds.

Hiring & High-Performing Teams: Using frameworks like Bullseye Hiring to ensure your next hire is your best hire. Episodes focus on building autonomous teams that own their outcomes and drive results without requiring constant oversight or micromanagement.

Scaling & Effective Operations: Refining the machine and building well-run systems to ensure the business can grow simply and sustainably. Lauren breaks down the strategic work that creates the leverage and capacity you need to finally reclaim your time, your sanity, and your freedom. 

If you’re ready to stop operating and start owning, this is your prescription for a business that scales sustainably and finally having the freedom you started your business for.

Subscribe today to start making the shift with Lauren.

title: The Accessibility Guy Podcast
author: Shawn Jordison
description:
Where accessibility meets real-world application.

Hosted by Shawn Jordison, digital accessibility consultant, trainer, and advocate, this show dives deep into the world of inclusive design, accessible technology, and the policies shaping our digital spaces. Each episode features candid conversations with experts, advocates, and everyday changemakers working to make documents, websites, videos, and software usable for everyone, including people with disabilities.

We explore accessibility from every angle:

Laws & Standards – Section 508, WCAG, ADA, AODA, Colorado HB21-1110, PDF/UA, and other regulations that shape compliance.

Practical Solutions – Tools, workflows, and strategies for creating accessible PDFs, Microsoft Office documents, and multimedia content.

Assistive Technology – How screen readers, captions, keyboard navigation, and other tools transform digital access.

Real-World Stories – Insights from educators, government officials, designers, developers, and advocates who are making a tangible impact.

Listeners can expect a mix of professional insights and practical takeaways. If you work in higher education, government, K–12 districts, nonprofits, or small business, you’ll find actionable advice that’s clear, simple, and ready to implement.

Every guest answers our signature questions, giving you a personal look at how accessibility impacts their work and life. From small victories to big systemic changes, you’ll hear stories that inspire action and highlight why accessibility matters—not just as a legal requirement, but as a human right.

Shawn’s own background spans years of helping organizations meet accessibility standards, remediate documents, train staff, and navigate complex legal requirements. Through this podcast, his mission is simple: make accessibility less overwhelming and more achievable for everyone.

Expect episodes that break down technical concepts without jargon, uncover creative problem-solving approaches, and share resources you can put to use right away.

What you’ll get from this podcast:

Clear, plain-language explanations of accessibility standards

Step-by-step tips for document and web accessibility

Interviews with leaders in the accessibility space

Stories from people directly impacted by accessibility barriers—and solutions that worked

Regular discussions on new laws, technology updates, and best practices

If you’re ready to learn, be inspired, and take concrete steps toward making your content, technology, and workplace accessible, this is your space.

Subscribe now to The Accessibility Guy Podcast, because accessibility is more than compliance. It’s about connection, equity, and building a world where everyone can participate fully.

author: deiconsultingfirms
description: In this podcast, we explore how Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) can help organisations create healthier, fairer and more inclusive workplaces. The discussion also covers inclusion for Persons with Disabilities, LGBT+ employees, racial and cultural diversity, and neurodivergent talent.

title: KETE IKURA ~ Sacredly Woven Womb Wisdom
author: Waikuranuku.Indigenous
description:
Sacredly woven from the depths of te pŏ.. nourished in the womb of Papatŭanuku Earth Mother. 

Weaving through timelines within the toto of our Tipuna kuia. Grounded and held by Wāhine & honoured by Tane


Ikura our scared womb blood.


Journey with us as we navigate Aotearoa, sitting in sacred space with Kuia, wāhine, Womb keepers, tane as well as Health and Wellbeing Practitioners from many different hauora fields. 

Join us to hear how they are Honouring Cycles and Rhythms, sharing their lived experiences, instilling this with in their uri, healing whakapapa lines, and Creating Sustainable wholistic wellbeing for kohine, wahine and mama and how this helps create hauora for all.


We speak into many aspects of what it means to honour the sacred ,our natural cycles, wahine hauora & again how this serves all living beings.

description:
Living Your Dharma is a collection of short, practical episodes exploring timeless yoga wisdom in a relatable, everyday way. Each episode offers one simple teaching from Yoga, Tantra or Ayurveda to help you reconnect with yourself, shift your perspective, and move through your day with greater clarity and purpose. description: Beyond the Braiding Chair is where braiding culture meets business, education, and community. Hosted by Diena Diallo, master braider and founder of DSN Braiding and Braidpedia, this podcast pulls back the curtain on the real stories and real growth that shape careers in the braiding world.  Diena sits down with clients, students, fellow professionals, and friends for honest conversations about craft, entrepreneurship, and the moments that happen beyond the chair itself. We believe change starts with people willing to make waves. Hear their stories, learn from their work, and be part of what comes next.

title: Forest Stories
author: StoryBooth
description: From the World Forestry Center and the U.S. Forest Service comes Forest Stories.  Celebrating 250 years of America’s forests and 60 years of the World Forestry Center’s mission to educate and connect people with the natural world.  Hear personal reflections, and stories of how forests have shaped lives—creating a living archive of human connection that will inspire support for our forests for generations to come.

title: Between the Lines
author: Cheralyn Darcey
description: An old-fashioned radio serial for modern ears. Lucy Halloran, 58, divorced, is working in a Newcastle bookshop when a mysterious Thursday regular offers to help her finish the novel she's spent thirty years not writing. His only condition: no questions about who he really is. Lucy has read every one of his books. She knows the charming man is never what he seems.

title: Wait...That's Science!

author: Elisa Harris

Welcome to Elisa Creates Stories, a magical storytelling podcast for children.
Each story is lovingly written and narrated by Elisa, bringing imaginative adventures, gentle bedtime tales, and heart-warming moments designed to spark creativity and help little listeners relax.

title: APEXIA Insights
author: APEXIA Consulting Corp.
description:
This is my very inteAPEXIA Insights is a leadership and management podcast for people who want results without losing the human element.


I’m Weam Abbas, founder of APEXIA Consulting—a firm specializing in leadership and management development, soft skills, and protection-focused professional training. Over the years, I’ve worked at the intersection of people, performance, and real-world pressure: what actually happens when teams are stressed, systems are messy, and decisions matter.


This show is built for leaders, managers, and professionals who are tired of leadership advice that sounds great… but collapses the moment you try it on a Monday morning.


On APEXIA Insights, we explore:


  • leadership psychology and human behavior in organizations
  • communication that works under pressure
  • trust, accountability, and culture (how they’re built—and how they’re quietly destroyed)
  • decision-making, conflict, and performance
  • change leadership and resilience
  • modern leadership realities, including AI and the future of work


You’ll get clear frameworks you can apply immediately—especially The APEXIA CALM Framework: Clarity, Accountability, Language, Modeling. When leadership gets noisy, we go CALM.


Expect calm, practical teaching, a little humor (sometimes the workplace deserves it), and occasional deep dives into academic research—without turning the show into a lecture.


If you care about becoming the kind of leader people trust—and the kind of workplace people don’t need to recover from—this is for you.


Listeners can expect:


  • practical frameworks (clear enough to remember, strong enough to run a team on)
  • leadership psychology + human behavior explained plainly
  • research references you can look up and verify
  • calm delivery with a hint of humor and “real talk”
  • episodes designed for both audio and video platforms


Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/privacy for more information.

Each episode, we dig into the world of Latine, BIPOC, and indie literature: the newest releases worth your time, the quiet gems getting passed over, and the real conversations happening around book bans and the fight to keep these stories on the shelf.

You'll hear honest reviews and recommendations, chats with indie authors, and spotlights on the small bookish businesses keeping community-first storytelling alive — all from someone who reads (and sells) this stuff for a living.

Pull up a chair under the moon. Let's talk about what we're reading, why it matters, and who's being left out of the conversation.

title: The World As My Laboratory - Shantoo Gurnani's Tryst With Science by SPARROW
author: Sound & Picture Archives for Research On Women (SPARROW)
description:
A young girl in Karachi whose family did not allow her to study beyond the fourth standard; an eager girl who read all the papers especially for information on new discoveries in science and worried that there would be nothing left for her to discover if they did not let her study further; a twenty-two year old girl walking on the streets of Bombay with her brother after Partition, to find out if the city could give succour to her large family of five sisters and five brothers; a research scientist who never got tired of her laboratory; a sanyasi who wants to find out the nature of the subject since as a scientist she can grapple only with the objective world.
These images of strength and resilience emerge from the narration of Shantoo Gurnani - a narration that informs us about educational choices women made in the thirties and forties and the careers in science opening out for women in the early half of the century.
Written and presented by Sound & Picture Archives for Research On Women (SPARROW).
Voiced by Shoa Hussain.
Produced by OfSpin Media Friends.
Learn more about SPARROW here: https://www.sparrowonline.org/

description:

From the music and moments that influenced her formative years to the experiences, lessons, opinions, and stories that followed, Robin invites you to pull up a chair and listen in as she reflects on the people, places, and memories that helped shape who she is today.

With a little laughter, a little nostalgia, and plenty of stories along the way, Notes from Rockin Robin is a celebration of where we come from, what we’ve learned, and the memories that stay with us.

So grab your favorite drink, turn up the volume, and take a trip down memory lane with Rockin Robin. 🎙️✨

title: M&A Matters
author: mandamatters
description:
What do businesses and investors need to consider when navigating M&A transactions across the Middle East?

Welcome to M&A Matters, a podcast series examining the legal, regulatory and commercial issues that can influence how transactions are structured, negotiated and executed across the region.

Hosted by Henry Storrar, Partner in our Corporate team, the series brings together specialists from across the firm to provide insight into the issues that sit alongside the core corporate aspects of a transaction.

From tax and regulatory considerations to due diligence, risk allocation and transaction structuring, each episode focuses on a different area of M&A and what businesses and investors need to consider when approaching a transaction.

The series explores the issues that can arise at different stages – from evaluating an opportunity and determining the right structure to negotiating appropriate protections, completing the transaction and planning for a future exit.

Whether you are considering an acquisition, investment, joint venture or wider corporate restructuring, M&A Matters provides practical perspectives on the issues that can influence transactions across the Middle East.

🔔 Follow the series for the latest episodes.

title: Career Talk With Mario Saucedo

description:
Career change doesn’t mean starting over.


Career Talk with Mario Saucedo helps experienced professionals recognize the value they have already built, navigate career change, and make their next move with greater clarity and confidence.


Drawing from more than 15 years of experience across airline, travel, telecom, media, banking, and technology leadership, Mario shares practical guidance shaped by deliberate career moves, unexpected transitions, and a layoff that ended a decade-long chapter.


Each episode explores transferable skills, career clarity, professional positioning, job-search strategy, leadership, and the realities of moving into a new role or industry.

Whether you’re recovering from a layoff, feeling stuck in your current role, considering a move into a different industry, or sensing that it’s time for something new, Career Talk will help you recognize what travels with you—and act on it.


You are not starting over. You are building on everything you have already created.

title: The Profound Parent Podcast - with Dr. Dana Johnson
author: Dr. Dana Johnson
description:
The Profound Parent Podcast

Parenting a child with profound autism and complex support needs requires a depth of knowledge, courage, and advocacy that few people truly understand. The Profound Parent Podcast is for parents raising children with high support needs—including nonspeaking or unreliably speaking children—and navigating a world that doesn't always know how to see the whole person.

A Profound Parent isn't defined by a diagnosis. They're defined by the depth of knowledge, resilience, and fierce advocacy they develop along the way.

This podcast explores what it really means to raise a child with profound autism, complex support needs, and significant communication challenges while holding two truths at once: a child can have profound, lifelong support needs and be thoughtful, intelligent, curious, and capable of learning.

Difficulty demonstrating ability is not the same as an absence of ability.

Each episode brings you real stories, practical tools, honest conversations, and mindset shifts for navigating communication, advocacy, education, AAC, daily life, and the complicated realities of high-support-needs parenting. We talk about what it means to presume competence, support communication, understand behavior, and advocate fiercely—even when the world underestimates your child.

Because understanding profound support needs should never mean underestimating the person.

The Profound Parent Podcast: Understanding profound needs without underestimating the person.

title: Illinois Hell Hole
author: Matt Brookens
description:
"A 'movie for your ears,' with immersive soundscapes, music and the kind of
engaging performances that would be at home in a big-budget theatrical
release." — Illinois Times

HORROR COMEDY | FULL-CAST AUDIO DRAMA | NEW EPISODES EVERY SATURDAY THROUGH OCTOBER 24 — START WITH EPISODE 1

A snarky, entitled emo musician inherits his parents' farm and discovers a
bottomless pit that grants wishes — but only when suckers are chucked in. Now
his WILDEST DREAMS are just a few "accidents" away.

Today, Ned Fischer's precious little life pretty much crapped the bed: Dumped by his girl, booted from Mothers of Misery, and let go by his boss who is a "Dickless dick." "Could this day get any worse?," he moans. RING RING. – Mom and Dad's plane went down. No survivors. Everything is upside down.

Back in the Midwest to settle his affairs (ugh), he finds a liminal creepy farmhouse, a cousin with golden retriever energy, oh... and a BOTTOMLESS PIT to HELL in the middle of the corn field! At least drinks are cheap at The Busted Bottle.

Things go from bad to PLEASE STOP. After a freak "accident" involving the hole, (YIKES) a dark wish comes true. That's when an old-timey stranger in a vintage suit turns up with advice Ned didn't ask for. Ned rekindles some sparks with his old crush, Lenore... who just happens to have a boyfriend the size of a tank. Drowning in sorrows and not afraid to tell everyone, Ned turns to the town psychic. Moonglow doesn't have enough sage to ward off this Emo boy's DEMONS... which are freaking REAL and stalking him at night.

Can atheists go to hell? Ned's probably going to find out.

Darkly funny and viciously satirical, ILLINOIS HELL HOLE is a supernatural
fable about ego, and the price of getting something for nothing.

Nine episodes. Full cast. Immersive soundscapes. Best on headphones.

"This is in my top 10 audio dramas. It's such a good story, you will not be
able to put it down." — Dylan from Horror.Kult

For fans of What We Do in the Shadows, Beetlejuice, Tucker & Dale vs Evil,
Army of Darkness, and The Simpsons Treehouse of Horror.

Originally broadcast on NPR Illinois 91.9 FM.

Contains strong language and occasional violence.
